The absence of urinary symptoms and a normal urinalysis make infectious epididymitis less likely despite his sexual history. Key exam findings—right testicle elevated with a horizontal lie, absent right cremasteric reflex, and lack of pain relief with elevation (negative Prehn’s sign)—strongly point away from epididymitis and toward testicular torsion. The scrotal Doppler ultrasound demonstrating decreased blood flow to the right testicle provides objective confirmation. This is a surgical emergency requiring urgent urologic intervention to attempt detorsion and testicular salvage. 
DIAGNOSIS: Right testicular torsion.
